failures.triage_note: Root cause confirmed in code: DisputeService::open() (wp-sell-services/src/Services/DisputeService.php, lines 223-331) inserts the opening statement only into wpss_disputes.description (and wpss_disputes.evidence only if a $meta array is passed, which the REST create_item() path never does). It never inserts into wp_wpss_dispute_messages. get_evidence() (same file, line 607) - the sole source for the 'Messages & evidence' panel on both the member dashboard and (per the shared method) the admin dispute screen - only reads wp_wpss_dispute_messages, so a freshly opened dispute always renders 'No messages yet' until the first reply. Reproduced twice: once on stale QA fixture disputes (ids 69, 71) and once on a dispute opened live through the real 'Open Dispute' UI form on order 3515 (dispute id 379, deleted after verification, order restored to in_progress).
failures.expected: Per audit/journeys/02-dispute.md step 2: 'Messages & evidence shows the opening statement immediately. The text "No messages yet" must not appear.'
failures.actual: The opening statement shows correctly in 'Reason' and in 'Activity', but 'Messages & evidence' shows 'No messages yet. Add one below to make your case...' with zero rows in wp_wpss_dispute_messages for the dispute.

failures.triage_note: Security property (cannot mint unlimited tokens from a stolen token) DOES hold - the request is refused with 401. But the response code is the generic AuthController password-check failure (invalid_credentials) rather than the documented wpss_token_cannot_mint code that audit/journeys/08-mobile-app-session.md step 2 specifies. Likely the token-shape detection guard (recognizing our own minted 'username:secret' base64 tokens) either isn't wired into POST /auth/login's password check, or the generic password mismatch short-circuits before it runs. Low severity (no security impact, a client-facing contract/documentation mismatch only) but worth a quick check of AuthController::login() / AppTokenGuard for the missing branch.
failures.expected: 401 wpss_token_cannot_mint when a previously-issued token is passed as the account password to POST /auth/login.
